details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms developing across western South Dakota may intensify into a robust MCS in the coming hours. details.label: Discussion
details.text: Large-scale ascent continues to spread east across the central and northern High Plains based on recent GOES imagery with several clusters of high-based thunderstorms emerging from eastern MT into eastern WY and CO. More recently, a cluster of high-based thunderstorms has developed across far western SD in proximity to the western fringe of a moist plume that extends from the central Plains into western SD around a weak surface low analyzed south of the Black Hills. Over time, this convection should intensify as it continues to spread east into the moist air mass where MLCAPE rapidly increases into the 3000-4500 J/kg range. Additionally, the combination of southeasterly low-level winds to the north of the low with 30-40 knot mid-level flow aloft is supporting around 40-50 knots of effective bulk shear across the warm sector. This will likely promote organization of deepening convection over the next few hours - most likely into an MCS as cold pools continue to amalgamate and deepen. If an MCS emerges, the downstream environment will likely support severe gusts as high as 65-80 mph, and potentially a few embedded circulations given strong westerly low-level shear. Most high-res solutions over the past several hours have depicted some form of an MCS emerging out of the Dakotas this evening, though considerable spread is noted on precisely when and where such an MCS will emerge. Based on these observed trends, this cluster may develop into the anticipated MCS. Trends will continue to be monitored, and watch issuance will likely be required if the cluster continues to intensify

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered damaging winds remain possible this evening with a line of thunderstorms moving east-southeastward towards the Atlantic Coast

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A well-developed squall line with a history of producing scattered wind damage across southern/central VA will continue to track east-southeastward this evening. The airmass ahead of the line remains moderately unstable, with surface temperatures generally in the upper 80s to low 90s, and dewpoints in the 70s. Even though mid-level lapse rates remain modest, daytime heating has supported steepening of low-level lapse rates. This, coupled with around 30-40 kt of mid-level west-northwesterlies, will likely support scattered damaging wind potential with the line for the next couple of hours as it approaches the Atlantic Coast. A couple of cells that have developed ahead of the line across far southeast VA may also pose an isolated risk for severe hail in the short term. A local extension in area for Severe Thunderstorm Watch 558 may be needed for the rest of southeast VA based on current trends

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorm development is anticipated in the coming hours across northern Indiana and western Ohio. Although timing remains uncertain based on latest satellite trends, watch issuance will likely be needed given a favorable convective environment for severe thunderstorms

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Air mass recovery has been ongoing across IN and western OH in the wake of convection earlier today with temperatures warming well into the mid to upper 80s and dewpoints increasing into the mid 70s. This low-level destabilization, combined with eastward advection of steeper mid-level lapse rates, are supporting a corridor of extreme buoyancy with MLCAPE values estimated to be between 4000-5000 J/kg. Upstream, a subtle mid-level vorticity maximum is noted across central IL has been supporting weak convection across northern IL over the past few hours. Additional thunderstorm development appears likely as ascent associated with this weak disturbance spreads east towards the buoyancy axis. Although the region remains on the southern periphery of a 40-50 knot mid-level jet, regional VWPs show 25-30 knot flow between 5-7 km, which is supporting adequate hodograph elongation for effective bulk shear values on the order of 25-35 knots - sufficient for organized convection, including a few supercells. Exact timing of when robust/intense convection develops remains uncertain with latest GOES imagery showing limited vertical growth of low-level cumulus. Additionally, recent high-res solutions also shows disparity regarding the timing of convective initiation. Regardless, watch issuance will likely be required once thunderstorm initiation becomes apparent given the favorable convective environment

details.label: Summary
details.text: A gradual increase in the severe wind threat may occur this afternoon and evening, with Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A mid/upper-level anticyclone remains anchored over the Four Corners this afternoon, with modest (around 10-20 kt) easterly mid-level flow persisting across parts of NM/AZ per recent VWPs from KEMX. Modifying the 18Z observed sounding from PHX for current surface conditions shows a very well-mixed boundary layer through low/mid levels, with around 1600 J/kg of MLCAPE and ample DCAPE as well. This agrees with latest mesoanalysis estimates, which suggest around 1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE is present across the lower elevations of southeast/central AZ. Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms have recently developed over the Mogollon Rim in east-central AZ and the higher terrain in southeast AZ. Recent trends in short-term model guidance remain unclear regarding potential for this activity to increase in coverage through the remainder of the afternoon, and whether one or more bowing clusters eventually develops westward into the lower deserts over the next few hours. Regardless of this continued uncertainty, the thermodynamic environment appears favorable for severe gusts if convection can grow upscale. Watch issuance is possible, and will largely depend on convective trends

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of severe wind gusts and hail will increase from west to east during the next few hours. A watch may be needed relatively soon for parts of the area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated high-based thunderstorms are evolving along a lee trough extending from the NE Panhandle southward into northeastern CO, and storm coverage should continue to increase as a subtle midlevel wave approaches the area from the west (per recent WV loops). Over the next few hours, this activity will spread eastward into a a plume of middle/upper 50s dewpoints and steep deep-layer lapse rates, which are contributing to a moderately unstable air mass. This, combined with an elongating and mostly straight hodograph, should support some convective organization/cell splitting. While severe hail will be possible (especially in the earlier stages of convective intensification), the primary concern will be an increasing risk of severe wind gusts with any clustering that occurs. A watch may be needed relatively soon for parts of the area
